claim: A message between agents is accepted only if it is signed by a sender the recipient knows, addressed to that recipient, and carries a sequence number strictly greater than the last one accepted from that sender.

steps.label: signed by a known sender, addressed here, sequence 1
steps.evidence: signature covers sender, recipient, sequence and payload

steps.label: the same message delivered a second time
steps.note: A replay is a message that was genuine once. A signature check alone cannot see it.

steps.label: a genuine message addressed to a different agent
steps.detail: addressed to auditor-agent, I am worker-agent
steps.note: Signed, genuine, and not for me. Acting on it is the agentic equivalent of opening someone else's post.

steps.label: that intercepted message re-addressed to me
steps.evidence: fails as signature_invalid, because the recipient is signed too
steps.note: This is why the signature covers every field the recipient will act on, not just the payload.

steps.label: a message from an agent whose key I do not hold
a gap in the sequence, after a dropped message
steps.note: Refusing to move past a gap would let one lost message wedge the channel forever. What is refused is a sequence already seen.
